messages:
Anya: FYI - NVD published CVE-2026-2101 affecting async-jsonrpc <=1.2.2, remote deserialization leading to RCE when running the agent with elevated creds. https://nvd.example/CVE-2026-2101
Kevin: thx. where do we use async-jsonrpc in prod?
Anya: devops-agent (our node-side helper) pulls configs and executes tasks; used in Dedicated node images and customers running Private on-prem packages. Hosted API runtime does NOT bundle devops-agent.
Maria: so hosted customers safe, dedicated+private potentially exposed. any exploitability details?
sec-bot: automated-scan: 14 hosts in Dedicated pool have devops-agent v1.0.0 (async-jsonrpc 1.2.2). 6 customer-managed Private clusters reported devops-agent present. CVSS 8.1, unauthenticated payload requires access to agent's control port (default 127.0.0.1:7001) OR a misconfigured proxy.
Oliver: can confirm our Dedicated bootstrap installs agent on worker nodes for autoscaler hooks. control port bound to localhost but we have had proxies in a few clusters (internal ticket #7842).
Kevin: can customers easily mitigate short-term?
Maria: mitigation options: 1) firewall/iptables to block access to 7001; 2) set AGENT_MODE=disabled and restart node; 3) upgrade async-jsonrpc to patched 1.2.3 (recommended).
Anya: proposed triage: classify as P2 (high) for Dedicated/Private due to potential exploitable configs. P3 for hosted (no action). Recommend immediate customer notification for Private installs + opt-in emergency patch for Dedicated nodes we manage.
Kevin: timeline proposal: - tonight: emergency blocker checklist + canary patch 1 node in pool A - tomorrow AM: expand to 20% pool canary, run smoke and key rotation tests - 48h: full rollout for Dedicated non-burst pools - Private: provide KB + hotfix patch and offer support sessions.
Oliver: can we avoid KMS key rotation? devops-agent uses KMS unwrap for short-lived creds. If attacker gets code exec they could request token unwrap, so rotate the affected key material after patch. I suggest marking rotations as required for private customers who can't patch quickly.
Maria: communication draft: short risk note, mitigation steps (disable agent, firewall, upgrade), signpost support link. For Dedicated customers we manage, schedule outage window 2am-4am PT next Tue. Include canary status and rollback plan.
Anya: rollout playbook (short):
```
1) Canary node: ssh -> systemctl stop devops-agent; upgrade package: `pip install async-jsonrpc==1.2.3` or deploy new image; restart and run smoke tests
2) Verify audit logs and no unexpected agent outbound requests for 30m
3) If green, scale to 20% nodes, run integration jobs
4) Rotate KMS wrapping key for tokens used by agent (coordinate with infra ops)
5) Communicate completion and CVE advisory
```
Kevin: +1. Add an automated check to the deploy pipeline to fail if any image contains async-jsonrpc <=1.2.2. Also add an alert to infra dashboards for unexpected binds to 7001.
deploy-bot: deploy-plan-schedule: canary-start=1957860000 canary-end=1957861800 owner=@Oliver
Oliver: I'll take lead on Dedicated rollout. Maria -> can you own the customer comms + KB? Kevin -> infra alerts and pipeline gate? Anya -> coordinate Private outreach & support schedule.
Maria: on it, will draft and share in #announcements for legal review before send.
Anya: thanks all. I'll start the private customer list and prioritize engagements by customer tier (enterprise customers flagged for immediate outreach). We'll update this thread with canary results. :thumbsup:
